subject: Budget range validation - PayBridge monthly spend band
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paybridge.com>
Cc: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@paybridge.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & quick budget check - PayBridge

Hi Alex / Morgan,

Thanks again for jumping on the call this morning - really helpful to understand how PayBridge plans to use LLMs across customer support and payment reconciliation. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size pricing options correctly: 

Recap from call:
- Primary workloads: chat-based support (generation-heavy) and backend reconciliation (embeddings + reranking).
- Expected steady-state: ~50M tokens/month (rough split estimate below).
- Peak concurrency: up to ~20 concurrent users during batch runs; latency SLOs for support flow: < 300ms p95.

Questions / asks:
1) Can you confirm a high-level token split (generation vs embeddings)? Even a 70/30 or 60/40 estimate helps.
2) Do you have a target $/1M tokens or a monthly budget band you're comfortable with? For example, are you targeting $800-$1,200 / 1M tokens or looking for committed pricing tied to a minimum monthly spend?
3) Procurement thresholds: what approvals or PO minimums are required on your side (e.g., PO > $50k, legal review needed)?

I attached a very small usage_estimate_template.csv you can fill quickly if that's easier. Once we have the token split and budget band I'll loop in Marissa and our finance lead (Dylan) to sketch a committed pricing option and procurement path.

Next steps: if you can reply with the 3 items above by end of day tomorrow we'll put together 2 pricing scenarios (pay-as-you-go vs 6-12 month commitment) + a SOW draft for procurement.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0138

Attachment: usage_estimate_template.csv (CSV stub)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paybridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Cc: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@paybridge.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & quick budget check - PayBridge

Thanks Rishi - great call. Quick answers below and attaching our initial usage snapshot.

1) Token split (best current guess): ~60% generation (chat responses) / 40% embeddings + reranking.
2) Expected volumes: 50M tokens/month steady-state, with the option to scale to ~120M in Q4 if the pilot goes well.
3) Target unit economics: our internal finance model is showing we need around $900-1,100 / 1M tokens to hit our unit targets, but we were hoping committed pricing could get us down to ~$750 / 1M on a 12-month committed band.
4) Procurement thresholds: Procurement requires formal SOW + PO for anything > $25k; legal review kicks in for contracts longer than 6 months or with data residency clauses.

Attached: PayBridge_initial_usage_report.pdf (usage snapshot + sample request distribution). Happy to hop back on a short call if you want to walk through the breakdown.

-Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, PayBridge
alex.chen@paybridge.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paybridge.com>
Cc: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@paybridge.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & quick budget check - PayBridge

Alex - appreciate the detail and the attachment. A few clarifying items so we can narrow pricing options: 

- On the 60/40 split: is the 60% generation mostly short chat responses (~30-150 tokens per reply) or are you expecting longer completions for reconciliation notes (~500+ tokens) for some flows? That impacts effective per-token cost.
- For the Q4 scale (120M): is that contingent on a successful pilot/beta or more committed based on roadmap? If it's contingent, we should model a staged commitment.
- Procurement threshold of PO for > $25k is good to know. On our side, to access committed discount tiers we normally map discount bands to monthly committed spend bands (example bands below):
  - Band A: $0-$50k/mo - pay-as-you-go / minimal commit
  - Band B: $50k-$150k/mo - tiered discounts (~10-20% depending on term)
  - Band C: $150k+/mo - deeper discounts / enterprise pricing and SLA options

Given your $750 target on 12-month commit: if you can commit to Band B mid-point (~$100k/mo) we can likely get ~15% off pay-as-you-go rates which would move you toward that target. I'll ask Dylan to confirm exact thresholds and approval paths.

If you're okay, I'll draft two quick scenarios: (1) 6-month pilot with a $50k/mo commit and (2) 12-month production commit at $100k/mo. I'll include expected effective $/1M tokens for both based on your 60/40 split and token-length assumptions.

Thanks - Rishi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: PayBridge budget band ask and procurement note (PB-2026-1072)

Marissa / Dylan - forwarding PayBridge responses (see attached report). Key takeaways:
- Steady-state: ~50M tokens/mo, potential to 120M in Q4 if pilot converts.
- Token mix: ~60% generation (mostly short chat, but may have bursts of longer completions), 40% embeddings/rerank.
- Procurement: PO required for > $25k; legal review for > 6 months or data residency clauses.
- Their target is ~$750 / 1M tokens on a 12-month commit, current internal model tolerates $900-1,100.

Ask: can you confirm the discount bands we can offer for Band B (~$50k-$150k/mo) and the approval path for a 12-month committed pricing that hits ~$750 / 1M? Also, if we need to structure the SOW to avoid extended legal review (e.g., limit initial pilot to 6 months), recommend language.

I've attached the usage snapshot and my suggested two scenarios (6-month pilot @ $50k/mo; 12-month commit @ $100k/mo). If you think 12-month at $100k/mo can get to $750 / 1M we can propose that to Alex and ask procurement for a PO pathway.

Thanks - Rishi

Attachment: PayBridge_initial_usage_report.pdf, SOW_draft_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@paybridge.com>, Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@paybridge.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & quick budget check - PayBridge / next steps

Thanks Rishi - read through. Quick suggested approach:

1) Offer two formal options to PayBridge (presented in a single email + SOW):
   - Option A (Pilot): 6 months, $50k/mo committed, flexible uplifts, standard hosted T&Cs. Effective target ~ $950 / 1M tokens given pilot term.
   - Option B (Production commit): 12 months, $100k/mo committed, 15% committed discount + 1% additional discount for upfront annual prepay. Effective target ~ $760 / 1M tokens (based on assumed 60/40 split and current model).

2) Procurement path: since their PO threshold is $25k, they can issue a PO for Option A without deep legal review. Option B (12-month commit) will trigger legal, but we can include a limited data residency clause and an initial 30-day escape for either party to limit legal friction - Scott (legal) usually accepts that for enterprise pilots.

3) Next steps: Rishi - send Option A & B to Alex with the SOW_draft_v1.pdf and include the HubSpot deal link. I'll prepare the formal pricing sheet and a DocuSign-ready SOW if they signal preference.

Cc: Alex / Morgan - if you have a preference between Option A vs B or timing constraints for Q4 scale, let us know. Happy to set a short alignment call this week.

-Marissa
